algorithm: Deterministic stub generation keyed by prompt hash, scored by a rubric heuristic over topic terms, required words, and length bounds.
complexity: O(V*I) for V variants over I test inputs; scoring is linear in response length.
data_flow_ascii:
template + variables -> render_template -> prompt
prompt -> stub_generate (hash-keyed canned content) -> response
response + rubric -> score_response -> 0..1
variants x inputs -> run_variant -> print_table comparison
description_sentence: A prompt template playground that substitutes variables into templates, runs A/B variants over seeded test inputs, and scores them with a rubric heuristic.
failure_note: Missing variables are left as literal {placeholders} in the prompt so a typo shows up visibly instead of crashing.

functions.desc: Substitute {placeholders} with variables; unknown keys stay literal.

functions.desc: The A/B prompt variants sharing the same variable slots.
functions.name: build_variants

functions.desc: Seeded test inputs: topic plus a sampled question each.
functions.name: make_inputs

functions.desc: Deterministic stand-in model: prompt hash picks canned content.
functions.name: stub_generate
functions.signature: stub_generate(prompt: str, variant: str, topic: str) -> str

functions.desc: Heuristic 0..1 score: topic term, required words, length bounds.
functions.name: score_response

functions.desc: Run one variant over all inputs; returns per-input scores.

label: prompt_playground
output_shape: Prints rendered prompt samples, a variant-by-input score table with averages, and the winning variant.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that A/B tests prompt variants over seeded inputs and scores them with a transparent rubric.

qa.a: A zlib CRC32 hash of the prompt picks canned sentences, so the same prompt always yields the same response.
qa.q: How does the stub model work?

qa.a: One point for the topic term, one per required word found, one for staying within the word-count bounds, divided by the total.
Swap stub_generate for a real model call; the rendering, scoring, and table code stays the same.
qa.q: Can this drive a real model?

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python that renders prompt templates, runs A/B variants over seeded inputs, and compares them with rubric scoring.
run_notes: --inputs sets the number of seeded test questions; the rubric lives in build_rubric().
scaling_note: The loop is single-threaded and suits hundreds of inputs; thousands would want batched or async model calls.
storage_note: No persistence: inputs, prompts, and scores are regenerated from the seed each run.
tradeoff_note: The stub model makes the harness fully offline and deterministic, but real model behavior needs a live backend.
